subject: Historia
title: Swedish history and the rise of democracy
sourceSummary: How Sweden gradually became a democracy during the first decades of the 20th century — the development of the right to vote, the breakthrough of parliamentarism, the 'people's home' and Sweden's path through the world wars.

questions.prompt: In which year was the first Riksdag (parliamentary) election held in Sweden with universal and equal suffrage for both women and men?
questions.opener: Men's suffrage came a few years earlier — but it took a while before women could vote in an actual election.
questions.explanation: Universal suffrage for men was introduced in 1909, and the Riksdag decided on women's suffrage in 1919 — but the first election in which both women and men had universal and equal suffrage was held in 1921. 1809 is the year of Sweden's Instrument of Government, and the other dates are too late.

questions.opener: Think about whose support the government must have in order to remain in power.
choices: That the government must have the support of a majority in the Riksdag in order to remain in power
That the king alone decides which laws apply
That only the nobility have the right to vote in elections
That Sweden has no elected Riksdag at all
questions.explanation: Parliamentarism means that the government's power rests on the support of a majority in the Riksdag (parliament), rather than being appointed freely by the king. The breakthrough of parliamentarism in Sweden is usually dated to 1917–1918, when the king's power over the formation of governments diminished considerably.

questions.prompt: Which movement fought for better conditions for workers and came to shape Swedish politics for much of the 20th century?
questions.opener: Think about trade unions and the political party that grew out of them.
choices: The labour movement, with trade unions and the Social Democrats as its driving forces
The Agrarian Party (Bondeförbundet), with no connection to trade unions at all
The leadership of the Church of Sweden
The Swedish nobility
questions.explanation: The labour movement, organised through trade unions and the Social Democratic Party, fought for better wages, working conditions and political influence for the working class, and became one of the most influential forces in Swedish politics during the 20th century.

questions.prompt: What was the basic idea behind the concept of the "people's home" (folkhemmet), which became central to Swedish politics from the late 1920s onward?
questions.opener: Think about the word literally: Sweden as a shared home for everyone.
choices: That Sweden should be like a shared home where the state takes responsibility for citizens' security and welfare
That all Swedes should live in the same residential area
That the state should be abolished entirely in favour of private solutions
That only wealthy families should receive state support
questions.explanation: The "people's home" was an idea, associated in particular with the Social Democrat Per Albin Hansson, that Sweden should function like a shared home in which the state takes responsibility for citizens' welfare, security and equality — a foundation for the development of the Swedish welfare state.

questions.prompt: What official policy did Sweden pursue during both the First and Second World Wars?
questions.opener: Sweden did not take part militarily in either world war.
choices: A policy of neutrality, meaning Sweden did not take part militarily in the wars
Sweden joined the wars on Germany's side
Sweden joined the wars on the Allies' side
Sweden occupied Denmark during the Second World War
questions.explanation: Sweden pursued an official policy of neutrality during both world wars and did not take part militarily in the fighting, unlike neighbouring countries that were occupied. During the Second World War, however, Sweden made several concessions to Nazi Germany, which have been debated ever since.

questions.prompt: What was an important consequence of women gaining the right to vote in Sweden?
questions.opener: Think about which new voices could now be heard in politics.
choices: More women could take part in political decision-making and push issues such as gender equality
The right to vote was taken away again after a few years
Women automatically received higher pay than men
The right to vote applied only to noblewomen
questions.explanation: Women's suffrage gave women the opportunity to vote and later also to be elected to political office, which over time helped give greater prominence to issues of gender equality and women's rights in Swedish politics.

questions.prompt: Explain how Sweden developed from a country with limited suffrage into a full democracy during the early 20th century.
questions.opener: Go through the development step by step: from men's suffrage, via the breakthrough of parliamentarism, to women's suffrage.
questions.answer: Sweden's path to democracy proceeded in several steps during the first decades of the 20th century. In 1909, universal suffrage for men was introduced for elections to the Riksdag's second chamber, but women still lacked the right to vote. During and after the First World War, as social tensions and demands for reform increased, the breakthrough of parliamentarism took place in 1917–1918, meaning the government had to have the support of a majority in the Riksdag. In 1919 the Riksdag decided on women's suffrage, and in 1921 the first Riksdag election was held in which both women and men had universal and equal suffrage. Reform work then continued, including the expansion of the people's home and the welfare state.
steps: 1909: Universal suffrage for men was introduced for elections to the Riksdag's second chamber, but women still could not vote.
1917–1918: The breakthrough of parliamentarism meant the government had to have the support of a majority in the Riksdag in order to remain in office.
1919: The Riksdag decided on women's suffrage.
1921: The first Riksdag election was held with universal and equal suffrage for both women and men.
After the breakthrough of democracy, reform work continued, including the idea of the people's home and a growing welfare state.

questions.prompt: Summarise the key steps in Sweden's democratic development and Sweden's role during the world wars.
questions.opener: Think suffrage, parliamentarism, the labour movement, the people's home and neutrality.
questions.answer: Universal suffrage for men was introduced in 1909 · the breakthrough of parliamentarism took place in 1917–1918, meaning the government had to have the support of a majority in the Riksdag · women's suffrage was decided in 1919, and in 1921 the first election was held with universal and equal suffrage for women and men · the labour movement, with trade unions and the Social Democrats, became a driving force in Swedish politics · the concept of the "people's home" (from the late 1920s) was built on the idea that the state should take responsibility for citizens' security and welfare · Sweden pursued a policy of neutrality during both the First and Second World Wars and did not take part militarily in the fighting · after the world wars, Sweden continued to build out the welfare state during the 20th century.
